behaviors: Hub re-exports the owned claudemon model/window implementation; no second Rust table or resolver. Shared table is checked row-for-row in exact order and kind (contains/prefix/suffix). All28 concrete lookup cases preserve first-match precedence and explicit unknown rather than guessed capacity.

All12 marker and24 resolution cases execute the real owner: reported positive window, positive user override, requested1M selection, concrete table, then unknown. Zero/absent claims are omitted; disqualified claims fall through rather than guessing a replacement. The directly asserted200000 and204000 peaks retain200000;204001 returns unknown.

Legacy badge assertions map to the actual catalog contract: opus/sonnet/haiku200K, opus[1m]/sonnet[1m]/fable1M, with numeric contextWindow values. Concrete claude-opus-4-8-20260101 and claude-fable-5 are explicit shared lookup rows200000 and1000000. The production catalog uses that same re-exported lookup and numeric K/M formatting; no independent guessed badge table.

Contract nonempty/corpus guards are retained by exact table length plus positive lookup/marker/resolution floors. Existing owner CI additionally exercises canonical selection, wire inputs, argv and provider context defaults. No fresh external model specification or inference from occupancy was introduced by this review.
intentionalChanges: The active Rust resolver uses the established canonical model-selection boundary before requested markers, rejecting malformed identities that legacy substring helpers could accept. ASCII model matching and saturating arithmetic are the existing Rust owner behavior; this review certifies shared contract and exact legacy test assertions, not arbitrary malformed-Unicode or overflowing-u64 equivalence. Display helper internals are consolidated into the actual catalog instead of duplicating formatThousands.
